clue.text: Greasy stuff very foolish for American writer to eat

indicators.note: a word that eats another takes it inside, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer of tales and poems
mad means very foolish or crazy

explanation.surface: A hair product so silly that an American author is made to swallow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scented ointment for the hair, which is greasy stuff by nature.

clue.text: Headlong fall when important lady drops off edge

definitions.text: Headlong fall when important lady drops off edge

indicators.note: the lady falls away from the end of the word, so those letters are removed from its edge

parts.note: a purler is a heavy headlong fall, a cropper
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A grand lady topples over a ledge and takes a nasty tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops off edge' removes ER from the end of PURLER. The shortened word is itself an old noun for a heavy headlong fall, so the whole clue both builds and defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage the word names a heavy tumble or capsize, the same tumble a purler describes.

clue.text: Male facing stress when leaving US city

indicators.note: one piece sits facing the other, so the male letter goes in front
the word for when departs from the word for stress, so its letters are taken out

parts.note: emphasis means stress or weight
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A man confronts tension at the moment of departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes AS out of EMPHASIS, leaving EMPHIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Tennessee on the Mississippi, home of Graceland.

clue.text: Author in a state, one of the characters flipping over

indicators.text: one of the characters flipping over
indicators.note: one letter of the word is turned upside down, and a W inverted looks like an M

parts.note: Delaware is a US state

explanation.surface: A writer finds himself in a state, with one of his creations doing a somersault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one of the characters flipping over' turns the W of DELAWARE upside down into M. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter de la Mare was an English poet and novelist, author of The Listeners.

clue.text: Girl needs a soft drink, somehow going from do to do

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, for Diana
tonic water is a soft drink

explanation.surface: A girl wants a soft drink, wandering from one party to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do to do' looks like going from party to party, but do is the tonic-sol-fa note: the scale from do up to the next do.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatonic scale runs through the eight notes of the octave, from one tonic note to the same note above.

clue.text: Brilliant batting, say — one little old-style amateur?

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
to say is to tell
one is I, the roman numeral, a little single letter
in old cricket amateurs were Gentlemen, so a gent is an old-style amateur

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator praises a brilliant innings by an old-fashioned gentleman player.
explanation.walkthrough: English cricket once split players into professional Players and amateur Gentlemen, hence GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliant and clever are near synonyms for having a quick mind.

clue.text: Each party's beginning with trifle around small table

indicators.note: the trifle goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to toy is to trifle; a toy is a trifle

indicators.note: the beginning of the word party is its first letter

explanation.surface: At every party the start is a trifle served at a small table.
explanation.definitionFit: A teapoy is a small three-legged table, often used for a tea caddy.

clue.text: Whip up a story to deceive girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to tan is to beat or whip
a lie is a story told to deceive

explanation.surface: Someone concocts a fib to fool a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TAN into NAT. 'Whip up' looks like a single phrase meaning concoct.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalie is a girl's name.

clue.text: City woman offering opposing position

definitions.note: the answer is both a city on Lake Constance in Germany and a woman's name

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: A businesswoman from the City takes a contrary view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City woman' suggests a London financier, but each word is a separate definition of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the English name of Konstanz in Germany and also a female first name.

clue.text: Walk by river?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces stand side by side

parts.note: to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A query about strolling along a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramble is a leisurely country walk, and the clue's riverside stroll is one example of it.

clue.text: Distress when train set gets damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A child is upset when a toy railway gets broken.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to put into difficulty or hardship, to distress.

clue.text: A little comic, he contrived something lavatorial

indicators.note: contrived means artificially made up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A minor comedian produces some toilet humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable lavatory using chemicals instead of flushing water, as on caravans.

clue.text: Ultimately, ambiguities in puzzles may make one argue

definitions.text: Ultimately, ambiguities in puzzles may make one argue

parts.words: Ultimately, ambiguities in puzzles may make one argue
parts.note: puzzles with ambiguities lead to angry exchanges, and the puzzles themselves are named by the same two words

explanation.surface: Unclear clues end in arguments among solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: To have angry exchanges is to argue, and the puzzle type shares the same letters.

clue.text: Theatrical demand for silence right in manner of ancient Greeks

parts.note: hist is an old call for silence, like hush
Ionic is the style of the ancient Ionian Greeks, as in the Ionic order

explanation.surface: An actor calls for silence in a classical Greek theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic means melodramatic or theatrical in manner.

clue.text: School servant I dismissed may have left a mark

parts.note: a high school

indicators.note: the I is sent away, removed from the servant

parts.note: a waiter serves at table

explanation.surface: A school servant, sacked, may have left an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissed' removes I from WAITER, giving WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A flood tide leaves a tidemark on a wall, the familiar high-water mark.

clue.text: Irishman given a spooky experience abandoning church

indicators.note: the word for church is abandoned, removed from the other

parts.note: a seance, contacting spirits, is spooky
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irishman has an eerie experience and quits the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean is a common Irish man's name, the Irish form of John.

clue.text: Hotel man mixed something very dangerous for drinker

indicators.note: mixed letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A hotel barman mixes a dangerous cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Methyl alcohol is poisonous if drunk, causing blindness or death.

clue.text: Snide comment of Spain against its neighbour

indicators.note: against means up against, beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: Gibraltar, Gib for short, borders Spain
E is Spain's international vehicle code, from España

explanation.surface: A cutting remark from Spain aimed at Gibraltar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibe is a taunt or sneering remark.

clue.text: Officer in trouble caught by punch

indicators.note: the trouble is caught by the punch, held inside it

parts.note: biff is slang for a punch
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: An officer in trouble gets punched.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is a court officer who enforces orders, such as seizing goods.

clue.text: Solemnly declare situation when donkey had insatiable appetite

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
an insatiable eater ever ate, ate always

explanation.surface: A solemn statement about a time when a donkey was always hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'situation when' links: the situation is one where the ass ever ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To asseverate is to affirm or state earnestly.

clue.text: A mainstay thus set up is to the purpose

parts.note: a prop is a support, a mainstay

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read from the bottom, so reversed

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: A main support erected this way serves its purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means relevant, pertinent to the matter in hand.

clue.text: In some measure bullish, a person who would set the pattern?

indicators.note: In some measure says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone partly optimistic who would set the trend.
explanation.definitionFit: One who shapes things gives them their form or pattern.

clue.text: Potentially wretches with a gram being gained?

definitions.text: Potentially wretches with a gram being gained?

indicators.note: potentially means the letters could become something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: Dieters are miserable whenever even a gram goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' rearranges WRETCHES, WITH, A and G; 'being gained' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a slimming club, who might feel wretched at any weight put on.

clue.text: Carrier to deviate, avoiding double bend

indicators.note: avoiding means the bend is left out

parts.note: to stray is to deviate
S is shaped like a double bend, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A vehicle swerves to miss an S-bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray carries plates and cups.

clue.text: Those out for pleasure wanting seductive lady start to finish?

indicators.note: the starting letter moves to the finish of the word

parts.note: a stripper performs seductively

explanation.surface: Pleasure seekers want a striptease from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to finish' moves the S of STRIPPER to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Day-trippers are people out on excursions for pleasure.

clue.text: One to criticise smallest cut with little hesitation

parts.note: a snip is a tiny cut with scissors
er is a brief hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A critic makes a tiny cut after a moment's pause.
explanation.definitionFit: One who snipes makes sly critical attacks.

clue.text: Cover with new trees for trees destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed letters are broken up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Replanting where a forest was destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To replant woodland on cleared land is to restock it with forest.

clue.text: Bold attack in which one must keep quiet

indicators.note: in which one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: to flay is to attack harshly
sh is the call to keep quiet

explanation.surface: A daring assault during which one has to stay silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one must' is a link between the container signal and the quiet call.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and ostentatious, a loud bold style.
